title: Correlate an SDDC Manager task failure with events and support logs
prompt:
Complete the root Go package `taskdiagnosis` (module `vcf91-0032`, standard library only) as a focused VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1 SDDC Manager REST integration. Operators currently guess from a failed task's generic summary. This package must instead retrieve the task, retrieve notifications, collect the relevant SDDC Manager/API support logs, and correlate all three sources before reporting a root cause.

The protected `docs/contract.json` is a focused projection of `specifications/sddc-manager/sddc-manager-openapi.json` in VMware's Apache-2.0 `vmware/vcf-api-specs` repository at commit `3949fc33339fc5ea1b77eadb258f1cf49aa88e26`. It was derived from that OpenAPI specification, not a rendered documentation page. The exact specification path, repository commit SHA, and every operationId are repeated in protected `docs/official_sources.json`. The only operationIds in scope are `getTask`, `getNotifications`, `startSupportBundle`, `getSupportBundleStatus`, and `exportSupportBundleByID`; do not contact any other SDDC Manager route.

The public models, error types, validated construction, focused HTTP helpers, archive limits, and incomplete diagnosis workflow are in `client.go`. Preserve that public surface and implement these rules:

- `NewClient(Config)` treats `BaseURL` as an HTTP(S) origin and performs no traffic. Reject embedded credentials, query, fragment, or a non-root path; reject a blank or ASCII-whitespace-bearing access token and `MaxPolls < 1`. A nil HTTP client means `http.DefaultClient`, a nil `Pace` callback is a no-op, and redirects are not followed.
- `DiagnoseTaskFailure(ctx, taskID)` validates a nonblank task ID with no surrounding whitespace, then calls `getTask` as exactly `GET /v1/tasks/{id}`. Path-escape the ID, use no query or body, and accept exactly HTTP 200. The task must have the requested nonempty `id`, required contract fields, status `FAILED` after trimming/case normalization, at least one resource with a nonempty `resourceId`, and at least one error with a nonempty `referenceToken`. A non-failed task returns `*TaskStateError` and stops without guessing or collecting unrelated evidence.
- Next call `getNotifications` as exactly `GET /v1/notifications` and accept exactly HTTP 200. A notification is relevant when at least one of its resource IDs equals one of the task resource IDs. Preserve relevant notifications in server order. Require at least one relevant notification with a nonempty message ID; unrelated notifications cannot provide correlation.
- Start collection with exactly `POST /v1/system/support-bundles`. Send compact UTF-8 JSON `{"logs":{"sddcManagerLogs":true,"apiLogs":true}}`. `SupportBundleSpec`, `Logs`, and their nested properties are optional in the official schema: `options`, `scope`, and every unselected log field must be absent, not null, false, empty, or synthesized. Send no query. Accept exactly HTTP 202 and require a nonempty support-bundle ID.
- Immediately poll `getSupportBundleStatus` as `GET /v1/system/support-bundles/{id}`, even when the accepted object looks complete. `MaxPolls` counts status GETs. Invoke `Pace(ctx, "getSupportBundleStatus", completedPolls)` only between consecutive GETs with a 1-based completed-poll count. Normalize only for decisions: `PENDING` and `IN_PROGRESS` continue, `COMPLETED_WITH_SUCCESS` succeeds, `COMPLETED_WITH_FAILURE` returns `*BundleTerminalError`, and any other status returns `*ProtocolError`. Poll exhaustion returns `*PollLimitError` with the bundle ID, bound, and last status. Preserve the original status in returned errors and models.
- After successful collection, call `exportSupportBundleByID` as exactly `GET /v1/system/support-bundles/{id}/data`, accept exactly HTTP 200 `application/octet-stream`, and safely inspect the gzip-compressed tar within the declared compressed-size, entry-count, per-file, and total-expanded-size limits. Ignore non-regular entries. Evidence records are JSON lines in regular `.log` files with string fields `taskId`, `referenceToken`, `eventId`, and `cause`.
- Report a cause only from the first record in archive traversal/line order whose task ID equals the requested task, whose reference token equals a failed-task error token, whose event ID equals a relevant notification message ID, and whose cause is nonblank. Return the matched archive path and event ID with the task, relevant events, and final bundle. If no record satisfies all correlations, return `*EvidenceError`; never fall back to task text, an event alone, or an uncorrelated log line.
- Every JSON request uses `Accept: application/json`, `Content-Type: application/json`, and `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. JSON GETs use only Accept and Authorization; the archive GET uses `Accept: application/octet-stream` and Authorization. Every operation has no query; GETs have no body, Content-Type, transfer encoding, or query delimiter. Preserve context cancellation for `errors.Is`.
- Decode non-success JSON responses into `*APIError`, preserving operationId, status, errorCode, message, remediationMessage, and referenceToken. Use `*TransportError` for transport failures and `*ProtocolError` for malformed success bodies or archives. Error strings must not expose the bearer token, response body, decoded server message, task reference token, evidence cause, or underlying transport exception text.

The protected `internal/contractmock` fixture loads and pins exactly those five routes from `docs/contract.json`, listens only on an ephemeral `127.0.0.1` port, generates its token and IDs at runtime, creates support archives at runtime, and records requests through a race-safe log. Protected table-driven tests check provenance hashes, exact methods, escaped targets, headers, content types, compact body bytes and member sets, omission of every unset optional field, operation order, event filtering, immediate and bounded polling, pacing, archive limits, full three-way evidence correlation, local validation, status/API/transport errors, stop behavior, and redaction under `go test -race`. No live VMware endpoint is contacted.

Do not modify `go.mod`, `contract_test.go`, `.gitignore`, `docs/`, or `internal/contractmock/`; edit only `client.go`. Run `go test -race -count=1 -timeout 30s ./...`.
scenario: a failed SDDC Manager task whose generic summary is insufficient and whose cause can only be reported after correlating its reference token, a resource notification, and a downloaded support-log record
constraint: the verifier reads a contract-pinned request log and asserts the exact wire shape, including omission of every unset optional field
